title: The running athlete: stress fractures, osteitis pubis, and snapping hips.

sections.label: CONTEXT
sections.text: Pelvic stress fractures, osteitis pubis, and snapping hip syndrome account for a portion of the overuse injuries that can occur in the running athlete.

sections.label: EVIDENCE ACQUISITION
sections.text: PUBMED SEARCHES WERE PERFORMED FOR EACH ENTITY USING THE FOLLOWING KEYWORDS: snapping hip syndrome, coxa sultans, pelvic stress fracture, and osteitis pubis from 2008 to 2013. Topic reviews, case reports, case series, and randomized trials were included for review.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Collectively, 188 articles were identified. Of these, 58 were included in this review.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: Based on the available evidence, the majority of these overuse injuries can be managed non-operatively. Primary treatment should include removal from offending activity, normalizing regional muscle strength/length imbalances and nutritional deficiencies, and mitigating training errors through proper education of the athlete and training staff.
